# ankitsin.in — working rules

This is Ankit Sinha's personal site. Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` before touching anything; it is the source of truth for stack, routes, type system and SEO. This file is how to work on it.

**Also read `AGENTS.md` before writing any Next.js code.** It's regenerated by `next dev` itself and points at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` for the exact API surface of the installed Next.js version — this project's training data may be stale relative to it. If Next.js changes a convention, `AGENTS.md` wins.

## What this site is

A personal site for **Ankit Sinha**, who competes and posts online as **Haunts**. Backend and distributed-systems engineer. The site is set as a newspaper — New York Times print edition, not nytimes.com. Two jobs, in order:

1. A recruiter with ninety seconds finds the work, the skills and the contact details without hunting.
2. Searching "Ankit Sinha" or "Haunts" returns ankitsin.in, with his LeetCode, Codeforces, LinkedIn, X and Instagram clustered around it.

Everything else is subordinate to those two.

## The design brief

**Reference point:** a printed NYT broadsheet and NYT Magazine section openers, executed with the restraint of devingarcia.net. Professional first, striking second. Approved comp: `design/styleframes.html` — variant C, "the Hybrid."

**Non-negotiables**

- Newsprint ground, ink-black type. Not white, not grey — a warm off-white with a hint of yellow.
- Horizontal rules do the structural work: hairline, standard, thick. They separate; borders-on-boxes do not.
- A real multi-column grid with hairline gutters, collapsing to one column under 820px.
- All-caps letterspaced kickers above headlines. Bylines under them. A folio line with place, date and edition.
- Drop cap on the lead paragraph of a lead story. Once per page, never more.
- `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` anywhere digits stack.
- Running text at roughly 65 characters. Measure is not negotiable for the sake of filling width.
- **The one showpiece.** `/markets` — and only `/markets` — inverts to press black and sets its opener in condensed display type. That inversion is the site's single moment of volume. It works because it happens once. Do not give a second section its own showpiece, and do not reuse `PressBand` elsewhere; if a page seems to need it, the answer is no.
- **Markets leads on consistency, not rating.** Headline figures are the 64-day streak, 684 submissions, 131 solved — not the Codeforces number. Ratings appear below, small, honest. Revisit only when Codeforces clears roughly 1400.

**Forbidden**, because each one instantly reads as generic AI output and breaks the print metaphor:

- Rounded corners. `border-radius` is `0` sitewide. No exceptions.
- Box shadows, glassmorphism, gradient text, gradient heroes.
- Cards. Content is separated by rules and whitespace, the way a newspaper does it.
- Emoji as section markers or icons.
- Purple/blue gradients, neon accents, Inter, Space Grotesk.
- Scroll-jacking, full-page loaders, `100vh` heroes, fade-in-on-scroll as a default.
- Lorem ipsum. If content is missing, write a line marked `TODO(cv)` and say so.

**Motion:** almost none. A link underline that draws in on hover. Page transitions that are instant. Anything more has to be argued for, and `prefers-reduced-motion` always wins.

**Accent colour:** one, a printer's red (`#8C2A1E`-ish), used for kickers and the occasional rule. Spend it rarely.

**Facts come from the CV.** §1a of `ARCHITECTURE.md` is the complete sanctioned list of claims about Ankit — including his real CP figures as of 17 Sept 2026. Anything not in it does not go on the site.

## How to work on this repo

- **Plan before building.** For anything more than a single component, propose the approach and wait. Do not scaffold a feature and then ask.
- **Grid first, content second, polish last.** Never style a page before the column system it sits on exists.
- **One component, one job.** The inventory in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §5 is eleven components (eight shared, three Markets-only). Adding a twelfth requires justification in the PR description.
- **Never invent facts about Ankit.** No job titles, dates, ratings, company names or project claims that are not in the CV or in `data/`. Missing fact → `TODO(cv)` and flag it in your reply.
- **Never break the SEO layer.** Do not remove JSON-LD, change canonical URL handling, replace the `<h1>` with an image, or add client-side-only rendering to a content route.
- **Check the work.** After a visible change, run the dev server and look at the rendered page at 1440px and 390px before saying it is done.
- **Verify, don't claim.** If `npm run build` or the tests were not run, say so.

## Voice

Copy is written as newspaper copy: declarative, concrete, no adjectives that cannot be defended in an interview. "A modular monolith in Go" — not "a cutting-edge, scalable solution". Section names follow the paper (`Work`, `Markets`, `Profile`, `Writing`, `Letters`, `Archive`), but every one of them must also be obvious to someone who does not notice the metaphor.

## Commands

```
npm run dev        # localhost:3000
npm run build      # must pass before any commit
npm run lint
```
